t.7.4.1: Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, Rāma was filled with wonder that the origin of the Rākṣasas had formerly been in Laṅkā.
t.7.4.2: Then, shaking his head and gazing again and again at Agastya, whose form was like the three sacred fires, he spoke to him with a smile.
t.7.4.3: O blessed one, having heard from you that even in former times this Laṅkā belonged to the flesh-eaters, wonder has arisen in me.
t.7.4.4: We have heard that the Rākṣasas sprang from the lineage of Pulastya, but now you have declared that their origin was from another source as well.
t.7.4.5: Were they then mightier than Rāvaṇa, than Kumbhakarṇa, than Prahasta and Vikaṭa, and than the sons of Rāvaṇa?
t.7.4.6: Who was the ancestor of these, O Brahmin, what was his name, and what the strength of his austerities? And having committed what offense were they put to flight by Viṣṇu of old?
t.7.4.7: Tell me all this in detail, O sinless one. Curiosity has arisen in me; dispel it, as the sun dispels darkness.
t.7.4.8: Having heard those words of Rāghava, adorned with refinement, Agastya, slightly smiling in wonder, spoke to Rāghava.
t.7.4.9: Long ago Prajāpati, who arose from the waters, created the waters; then the lotus-born one brought forth beings to guard them.
t.7.4.10: Those beings, tormented by hunger, thirst and fear, approached the creator of beings as if in humble submission, saying, "What shall we do?"
t.7.4.11: Then Prajāpati, the giver of honour, addressing those beings with words and smiling as it were, said to them, "Guard them with diligence."
t.7.4.12: There some of them said, "We protect," and others likewise said, "We have worshipped." Thus addressed by the hungry and the not hungry, the Creator of beings then spoke to them.
t.7.4.13: Those among you who said, “We protect,” let them be Rākṣasas; and those among you who said, “We have worshipped,” let them indeed be Yakṣas.
t.7.4.14: There arose two brothers, Heti and Praheti, bulls among the Rākṣasas, subduers of their foes, who were like Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
t.7.4.15: Of the two, Praheti was devoted to righteousness and did not desire wives, but Heti then made the utmost effort for the sake of taking a wife.
t.7.4.16: He of immeasurable spirit and great wisdom himself took in marriage a maiden named Bhayā, the sister of Kāla, who inspired terror.
t.7.4.18: Vidyutkeśa, the son of Heti, whose radiance was like that of a blazing fire, grew up, mighty in splendor, like a lotus in the midst of the waters.
t.7.4.17: Heti, the foremost of Rākṣasas and best among those blessed with sons, begot on her a son who, it is heard, was known as Vidyutkeśa.
t.7.4.19: When that night-roamer had reached auspicious youth, his father then resolved to arrange his marriage.
t.7.4.20: Then Heti, bull among Rākṣasas, chose for the sake of a son the daughter of Saṃdhyā, who was equal to Saṃdhyā in splendor.
t.7.4.21: Reflecting, “She must certainly be given to another,” Saṃdhyā gave her daughter to Vidyutkeśa, O Rāghava.
t.7.4.22: Having obtained the daughter of Saṃdhyā, the night-roaming Vidyutkeśa took his delight with her, as Maghavan does with Paulomī.
t.7.4.23: Then, after some time, O Rāma, Sālakaṭaṃkaṭā conceived a child from Vidyutkeśa, just as a mass of clouds takes in water from the ocean.
t.7.4.24: Then that Rākṣasī went to Mandara and gave birth to a child whose splendour was like that of a rain-laden cloud, just as Gaṅgā brought forth the embryo born of Agni.
t.7.4.25: Having cast off that child she had conceived by Vidyutkeśa, she, eager for love-play, sported with her husband, forgetting the son born of her own body.
t.7.4.26: Abandoned by her, that infant, radiant as the autumn sun, put his hand to his mouth and cried out like the king of clouds.
t.7.4.27: Then the lord Hara, mounted on his bull and passing by overhead together with Umā, saw the crying child of the Rākṣasa.
t.7.4.28: Then Bhava, the destroyer of Tripura, out of compassion for Pārvatī, made that son of the Rākṣasa equal in age to his mother.
t.7.4.29: Having made him immortal, Mahādeva, the imperishable and undecaying, bestowed upon him a city that moves through the sky, out of a wish to do what was dear to Pārvatī.
t.7.4.30: Umā too granted a boon to the rākṣasīs, O son of a king: that conception should take place at once and birth at once as well, and that the child should at once attain an age equal to that of its mother.
t.7.4.31: Then Sukeśa, proud of the boon he had been granted, having obtained splendour from the side of the lord Hara, and having gained a city that moved through the sky, roamed everywhere through the sky, that greatly wise one, just like Puraṃdara.
